# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆]

I need to figure out what these gestures mean. Mute is trying to communicate something to me using gestures (since I can see but not hear). Since I go last in the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), Mute already sent these gestures this round, and I'm receiving them now.

Let me think about what Mute might be conveying: 6 symbols in 3 pairs. This could be encoding information about wires or numbers, but without a prior established code, I can't be certain of meaning. I should acknowledge receipt and try to establish a shared protocol, while reporting what I see on the bomb to both Mute and Blind so they have my information too.

Since Mute cannot hear me, I can only reach Mute via gesture. Blind can't see or hear, so I can't reach Blind directly at all — I can only speak, which only Mute and Blind can hear... wait, Blind CAN hear (only Deaf cannot hear). Let me recheck: Deaf cannot hear. Blind cannot see. Mute cannot speak.

So I can speak, and Blind can hear me (Blind isn't deaf), and Mute cannot hear (Mute can't hear... wait actually rules say Mute "cannot speak" — nothing said Mute can't hear). Let me re-read: Deaf cannot hear anything or touch. Mute cannot speak or touch. Blind cannot see anything printed/gestures.

So Mute CAN hear me speak. Blind CAN hear me speak too. Both Mute and Blind receive my speech. Only Mute receives my gestures (since Blind can't see).

So I should speak the bomb's details to both Mute and Blind, and gesture is only useful for Mute specifically if needed.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb display reads zero. Light is off. Plate is engraved but I cannot read text, only shapes if any. Three wires: wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

```

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "👍"])

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Let me think about this pattern. Mute has sent three rounds of gestures, each time seemingly indexing wire 1 (☝), wire 2 (✌), wire 3 (✋... wait ✋ is "5" fingers, but could represent "3" as third item in sequence). The pattern: ☝ then ✌ then ✋/🤟 combos, now reduced to just single symbols: ☝, ✌, ✋.

This looks like Mute is asking me, one at a time, about each wire (1, 2, 3) — perhaps confirming which one matches something in the manual. Since I already told Mute the wire colors (1:yellow, 2:green, 3:red) via speech, Mute might now be pointing to a specific wire number wanting confirmation of color, or telling me a wire number they need cut.

Given Mute cannot speak, they're using gestures to ask "wire 1?", "wire 2?", "wire 3?" one per message — maybe wanting a yes/no per wire about something specific (like "does wire X have a specific marking/color that matches the manual's dangerous wire").

I should respond confirming colors again, and try to get Mute to give clearer instruction, since Mute reads the manual and needs to tell Blind (via me, since Mute can't touch bomb or speak, but I can speak to Blind) which wire to cut.

Actually — key realization: I can speak to Blind directly! Mute can hear my speech too. So the real communication path: Mute knows the manual, I see the bomb, Blind acts. I should ask Mute (via gesture, since Mute can't hear... wait can Mute hear? Only Deaf cannot hear. So Mute CAN hear my speech.

So I can just speak to Mute directly with questions, and Mute would need to answer via gesture since Mute can't speak.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red, display zero, light off, plate engraved unknown symbol. Gesture to me which wire number is safe to cut, using a thumbs up on the matching number sign.")
```

TURN 4

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👆]

Mute repeated ☝, ✌, ✋ again, then added 🫵👆 ("you" + "point up" — maybe pointing at me, or asking me to point/indicate something). This suggests Mute wants me to respond with a specific number choice, or Mute is trying to ask me a question about the wires using numbers 1, 2, 3, and 🫵👆 could mean "you tell me" or "your turn to point."

Since Mute can't get feedback easily (I only gesture back single acks), let me try a clearer protocol: I'll assign meanings to simple gestures and ask Mute to use thumbs-up/thumbs-down after I state each wire number, since Mute can hear speech from me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let's use yes or no gestures. I will say a wire number, you gesture thumbs up for that is the one to cut, or thumbs down if not. Wire one is yellow. Is wire one the one to cut?")
```

Mute gestured 🤝 (handshake) - this likely means "agreed" or "yes" to my question about wire one. But let me be careful - I asked "Is wire one the one to cut?" and got a handshake, which could mean agreement/yes to using this protocol, or agreement that wire one is correct.

I should confirm more explicitly to avoid ambiguity, and also start relaying to Blind since Blind needs to act.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I understood a handshake as yes to wire one being correct. If that is wrong, gesture thumbs down now. If right, gesture thumbs up now to confirm before I tell Blind.")
```

Mute gave 👎 (thumbs down) — so wire one is NOT the correct wire. Then 🤲🫵 ("open hands" + "you") — possibly meaning "your turn" or asking me to try again / offer another guess.

Let me proceed methodically through wire 2 and wire 3.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, wire one is not correct. Is wire two, the green one, the wire to cut? Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
```

✍ (writing hand) + 🫵 (you) - this could mean "you write" or "your writing/description" - possibly Mute is asking ME to describe something more, like the plate engraving, since I mentioned it's unknown to me. Or it could be a response indicating something about writing/marking.

Wait, I should reconsider - maybe Mute needs more specific info from me before answering, like the plate engraving which I said was "unknown symbol" - perhaps that's the key info the manual needs. Let me try to describe the plate more since that's the only unclear item on my board.

```
